intro: The last part of section 34.4 turns to positive psychology, the science of what makes a life most worth living. It sets out what the field studies and its main empirical findings on happiness, relationships, work and positive institutions, then how its ideas reach clinical work: a broader picture of psychological health, assessment of strengths, brief exercises and the newer positive psychotherapies, with the chapter's own cautions.
objectives: Define positive psychology and explain why the chapter calls it a complement to problem-focused psychology, not a replacement.
List the robust correlates of happiness and the role of relationships, income, employment and religion as the chapter reports them.
Describe the four ways of responding to good news and the features of institutions where people flourish.
Explain Figure 34-48: assets and problems as two dimensions, and how traditional therapy, positive psychotherapy and promotion move a person.
Describe positive psychology assessment, why its measures are not diagnostic tests, and the counting blessings and signature strengths exercises.
State the five qualifications for using these techniques and what the evidence shows, using the update boxes on later meta-analyses and dimensional classification.
